candidates.prompt:
Read only the supplied current facts and return the component value described by the schema. Extract every explicitly stated service or work relation. Preserve the source roles: the worker is the person who performed the service, and the employer is the person or organization for whom it was performed. In active remuneration language such as “X paid A, B, and C for agricultural labor,” X is the employer and each coordinated payee is a separate worker. In passive language such as “A was paid for services performed for X,” A is the worker and X is the employer even when the payer is not stated separately. Do not propagate a kind, employer, period, or location across sentence boundaries.

Record role_basis and the exact source service term. Normalize only clear kinds such as agricultural labor or domestic service; otherwise retain the explicit generic term. Record a venue or geographic location only when the service clause itself states it. A venue category and a geographic location are distinct.

Service time must come from the service clause itself. A full source date may produce on_date; two explicit endpoints may produce closed_interval. A year explicitly modifying the service may be retained only as year_only, never converted into exact dates. A payment year, query workday, enrollment interval, attendance interval, or another event’s dates are not service dates. Thus “was paid in 2017 for services performed for X” has an unstated service period unless the service phrase supplies its own time.

Every positive record needs an exact nonempty substring of facts as its witness. Complete with an empty services array is allowed only after a finite scan finds no service-language cue. If service/work/employment language is present but its roles, coordination, attachment, or service-specific time cannot be read safely, return unread with services null. Never use a question, native query, legal outcome, statute, source identifier, earlier case, or reference answer. Do not emit is_query_service or any query-derived field.
candidates.rationale: Event-normalized representation. Each coordinated worker becomes a separate source-grounded service event, while role_basis and period_form preserve how roles and time were stated. This is straightforward for downstream consumers and makes ambiguous query alignment detectable without changing factual properties.

candidates.prompt:
Read only current facts and return the schema value, not a service_events wrapper. Represent each source service clause as one service_relations item. Keep coordinated workers together when one clause assigns them the same employer, service kind, location, and service period. For “X paid A, B, and C for labor,” workers=[A,B,C] and employer=X. For “A and B were paid for services performed for X,” workers=[A,B] and employer=X. For direct performance language, preserve the explicitly named performer and beneficiary/employer. Do not infer an employer merely from proximity.

The grammar field records which licensed role construction established the relation; it is factual provenance, not query identity. Preserve the explicit service_term and only normalize kind when its meaning is clear. Locations, venue categories, and countries must be attached to this service clause and must not be copied from education, residence, payment, or another service.

The period object is independent of identity. Use interval only for two service-specific full dates, date only for one service-specific full date, and year_only only when a year grammatically modifies the service itself. A payment year before “for services,” an annual amount year, a native workday, or enrollment/attendance dates do not modify the service and must leave period.status=not_stated. Never synthesize January 1 or December 31 from a year.

Use exact nonempty facts witnesses. Scan every sentence independently so that a following reversal of payer and worker or a different kind/period remains a distinct relation. If any service-language construction has unresolved coordination, attachment, voice, employer, or period, return unread and null rather than omitting it or claiming an empty complete scan. Complete empty is permitted only when the finite facts contain no service-language cue. No question, query, statute, source ID, answer, annotation, or previous example is available. Do not output query flags or legal conclusions.
candidates.rationale: Relation-preserving representation. A coordinated payment-for-service clause remains one observed relation with an ordered workers array and one shared, clause-local period. Expansion into native service events happens only in conversion, reducing accidental cross-worker or cross-sentence property copying.

value.rationale: Both revisions remove query identity from the factual view and make time provenance explicit. Candidate 1 emits one event per worker, which simplifies lowering. Candidate 2 preserves coordinated workers as one source relation and expands them only in conversion. Both keep payment years and enrollment dates out of service dates, treat unsupported service language as unread, validate exact facts witnesses, and align an opaque native service identifier only when source-observed roles uniquely match query roles.
